title: Dental floss
html_source:
dental floss must have been newly available in 1904 Ireland

credit for the invention of dental floss goes to a New Orleans dentist, who in 1815 began advising his patients to use a thin silk thread to clean between their teeth. The idea caught on, and in 1882 a company called the Codman and Shurtleft Company, based in Randolph, Massachusetts, began marketing an unwaxed silk dental floss. This was followed in 1896 by the first dental floss from Johnson & Johnson. The New Jersey-based J&J took out a patent for dental floss in 1898 that was made from the same silk material used by doctors for silk stitches
